Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Dr. Kaushal Jayendra Thaker,J.
Order on Criminal Misc. Bail Application

The instant bail application has been filed by applicant-appellant pending appeal against the judgement and order dated 21.11.2022 passed by Additional Sessions Judge 4th, Jaunpur in Sessions Trial No. 343 of 2013 whereby the learned Additional Sessions Judge has convicted the accused-appellant under Sections 498A IPC and sentenced him to undergo two years simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/- and in case of default in payment of fine, further to undergo three months simple imprisonment and acquitted in additional charges under Section 302/34 of IPC.

As far as Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act is concerned, the accused has been sentenced to one year simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.2000/-
and in case of default in payment of fine, further to undergo one month's imprisonment.
It is an admitted position of fact that the accused is in jail since 2015.
The punishment is of 10 years of incarceration.

sentences.text: From the facts, it appears that the accused has undergone about seven years and six months of incarceration till date.
Hence, the accused- appellant is entitled for bail.

Let accused-appellant, Sanjay Yadav, convicted and sentenced in the aforesaid Sessions Trial be released on bail during the pendency of the appeal subject to his furnishing personal bonds and two sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any unnecessary adjournment.
(ii)) The appellant shall not leave India without permission of this Court.
(iii) The appellant shall inform the change of address within 10 days, failing which the State shall be at liberty to request for cancellation of their bail.
(iv) Fine shall remain stayed.
As far as sentence is concerned, the same shall remain suspended during pendency of the appeal.
Order on Appeal List the matter when its turn comes.
